result.title: Crucible: Evaluating LLM Agents in Executable Chemistry Research Environments
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) perform well on chemistry knowledge benchmarks, which mainly assess question answering and isolated tasks. Chemical research, however, requires using specialized tools and interpreting their outputs to obtain chemically valid results. To address this gap, we introduce Crucible Bench to evaluate this ability across all four stages of the design-make-test-analyze (DMTA) cycle. The benchmark contains 1,078 tasks in 12 task families curated from 18 published datasets, covering molecular design, synthesis planning, experimental execution, closed-loop optimization, simulation, and analytical characterization. Agents access 75 domain-specific tools through the Model Context Protocol in seven isolated environments. Sandboxed graders verify the resulting synthesis routes, experimental protocols, and other outputs. Laboratory tasks use robotic simulators or previously measured experimental data. We evaluate 14 LLMs as agents and find that the best achieves an overall score of 0.545, with synthesis planning and closed-loop optimization emerging as the hardest domains. Overall performance does not predict optimization performance well: the model ranked twelfth overall achieves the highest score in closed-loop optimization. Error analysis also shows that agents often submit chemically invalid results despite running their tools successfully. Stronger models benefit more from tool access, but reliable use of chemical software remains a challenge that Crucible Bench can track as models improve.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Crucible Bench，在 DMTA 四阶段的可执行化学研究环境中用 75 个领域工具与沙箱评分器评测 14 个 LLM agent，发现最优模型仅得 0.545，且工具调用成功不等于产出化学上有效的结果。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作与视觉/多模态推理无直接关联，但其把「工具执行成功」与「输出是否被正确解释使用」分开评测，以及闭环优化中的多轮证据获取与停止决策设置，可能为诊断 latent 状态是否真正利用视觉证据提供评价范式线索，可供核查。
